query: What do Google Pixel 3 buyers report about SIM activation, unlocking, and compatibility with their carrier?
search_text: What do buyers report about SIM activation, unlocking, and compatibility with their carrier?

rows.text: NOT COMPATIBLE WITH ALL CARRIERS!. I purchased this device and tried to activate it with Sprint. When I entered the IMEI number, I was informed: "Sorry, but this phone can't be activated with Sprint service". I contacted Sprint Customer Service, and they confirmed with me that this phone is not compatible with Sprint.

It will be stupidly inconvenient (particularly if you are using a Sprint-reselling carrier and are not an actual Sprint customer) to get this device activated as Sprint probably won't have the MEID on file and will fight you with a million excuses when you ask to have it added to their database. Long version: This model of Pixel 3 is quite apparently the only one out of the whole 3 series that will activate on Sprint at all, albeit with complications. I was blissfully unaware of this carrier weirdness until I received my device, which arrived sealed and in perfect condition, went through the prompts to transfer my data, installed my SIM card and excitedly tried to activate it. I kept getting errors while doing online self-activation, and even the agent with my carrier (a small pay-as-you-go provider on the Sprint network) couldn't activate it remotely.

The phone I received was INELIGIBLE for activation with SPRINT. I purchased this phone to be used with my SPRINT plan. However, when I gave my IMEI/MEID number to Sprint, I was told that the phone was ineligible for activation and I would have to buy a new phone. I tried it both on the SPRINT website and in person at a SPRINT/T-Mobile store. I also bought the appropriate SIM card. I don't know if this is an issue with SPRINT, or with the phone--or both. The people at the Sprint store could not offer much info other than saying "that's the risk you take when you buy a phone from Amazon." I wasn't aware that buying a certified "renewed" phone from Amazon that said it was unlocked for "all carriers" was taking a risk.

Better than new but not truly unlocked. This phone was exactly like new and i love it! So it is released to accept sim cards from other carriers to get their service but it is not truly unlocked just released to do this. I am transferring my phone carrier from Metropcs to Google Fi and it will not work without getting a Google Fi sim card and as a Google Pixel 3 it should have automatically accepted Google Fi. It does not. So, you must purchase a small sim card for whichever carrier you choose to use. My phones carrier that released it is Verizon.

Not unlocked as advertised. Phone is listed on Amazon as unlocked but I received locked device for Verizon network. I can't activate my T-Mobile on it. Don't buy if you don't have Verizon, don't trust the unlocked part in the title.

New, unlocked, software upgradeable.. March 15, 2021. A previous reviewer left a very helpful tip about these being delivered with a Verizon SIM installed. When I received this, the sealed box had an overlay sticker saying New, Unlocked All Carriers. It does appear new and unused, all accessories are present and also new and unused. Before I turned it on, I checked and it did indeed already have a Verizon SIM installed. I removed it and put in a Mint Mobile SIM, and then powered it on. Set-up went fine, and it showed Mint service and made calls fine. It was running Android 9. I hit Check Updates, and it offered Android 10. No problems updating. Reset and checked update again, and it offered security updates. Repeat after each update. Eventually I got through the backlog of updates, it's now on Android 11 and the March 2021 security update. Completely current.

It's advertised as unlocked, but it is a locked phone.. This phone is locked into CDMA mode and is not able to be used by any carrier on their network today, regardless of SIM. It is a Verizon version of the Pixel 3, which means it is not unlocked and cannot be unlocked without rooting and ROM change. There's a reason this phone is so cheap, it's worth exactly zero dollars ($0).

Was not unlocked. Ad said that the phone would be unlocked for T-Mobile. I took it to T-Mobile to have them switch sim cards and activate and they showed me that the phone was still locked. Contacted seller and they said only thing I could do was return it which I did. Disappointed because I really wanted that phone.

NOT NEW, buyer beware of shady seller. WARNING: Product is advertised and packaged as new but is definitely used. Unlocked "new" Pixel arrived with a T-Mobile SIM card already installed. Buyer beware. Returning mine and getting a new 4a for the same cost from the Google shop. Edit: While we wait for our actually new phone from Google to ship, this Pixel 3 has started freezing and crashing. It has been lightly used for two weeks. I have a pixel 3 I purchased from Google when they first came out years ago and it has never had an issue. Absolutely awful seller.

Beware NOT fully UNLOCKED. Not fully unlocked. The device came with a Verizon SIM and no eSIM support. An unlocked Pixel has eSIM support and not locked to a particular carrier. The description should read Pixel 3 Verizon variant. Waiting on a Google Fi SIM. If it doesn't work I will be returning.

Beware: phone not unlocked. The phone is new as stated in condition however the seller Certified Tech USA has also advertised the phone is unlocked. That is not the case, it is verizon locked and upon speaking to verizon the device will automatically be unlocked if the device is paid for, which appatently this 3rd party has not and there is nothing else the carrier can do for me. I cannot review the product as it is unasable to me, however the review is for the seller.

Wasted time.. Phone was not unlocked! Seller was Tech Wholesale. I’m really annoyed that I wasted my time trying to figure out why it wasn’t accepting my SIM card before realizing it hardcoded to only accept Sprint. Save yourself the trouble and don’t buy these unlocked phones from 3rd party sellers.

Not unlocked. Funny this is unlocked but when I went to switch networks, straight talk compatible with my previous network, it says the IMEI isn't legit. now I don't have a phone and no clue what to do. thanks!

It is mentioned as unlocked and comes with Verizon sim.. They have mentioned unlocked but comes with Verizon sim. More it is not working properly. I want to return but I'm worried that my data transfered to google phone.

Not factory-unlocked, but Verizon-unlocked, with a locked bootloader.. This is a review for the one sold by the seller “Prime Mobility”. I gave it 3 stars, because the title says that it is a factory-unlocked version and the phone I received was NOT a factory-unlocked phone; It was a Verizon-unlocked phone. It was a phone that was originally locked to Verizon when it came out of the “factory”, and then, after being used by a user, it was unlocked by Verizon so that SIM from other carriers can be used. Factory-unlocked means being unlocked when it first came out of the “factory”. If you do not care about ROM's and do not know what "adb" is, then it does not matter. But Verizon-unlocked phones do not allow unlocking the bootloader, so you cannot install any custom ROM or even the developer preview version of Android from Google on it.
Locked to Verizon. Verizon locked, so an eSIM activation to Fi was not possible and had to get a SIM card. This is not an unlocked phone.

BOOTLOADER LOCKED -- IMEI 35XXX - Works with any carrier but can't load custom ROMs. While the device is technically carrier unlocked, the bootloader remains locked. These are not "UNLOCKED" phones -- these are Verizon versions of the Google Pixel phone. Google "UNLOCKED" pixel phones have an unlocked bootloader so you can load custom ROMs or official Google factory images. Verizon phones start with IMEI 35XX and the bootloaders are locked. This ad is misleading, misrepresenting the device that is being sold and false advertising.

Not unlocked. This seller is lying, this phone is not unlocked, hence the 2 stars. Phone itself is good, but I bought it with the intentions of modding it. But I can't, because it is carrier locked... Otherwise, I do like the phone. The battery in it is definitely old, so it doesn't last very long. I was able to find a replacement easily, though.

Unit was not unlocked. Was hard locked to Verizon.. I have purchased two of these phones from two different sellers, one was factory unlocked for carrier and network. This one was hard locked to Verizon. Needed unlocked non-verizon, so returned for easy refund. It would be a 5 star item but -1 star for advertising it as the unlocked version in the title.

Seller says Phone is unlocked but phone is locked to Verizon.. The product headline states it is "unlocked" So I felt very safe in assuming it wouldn't be locked to a carrier. But mine is locked to Verizon.
